Article Title: E100 cars get regulatory green light ahead of planned launches
Article Text:
Govt allows registration of flex-fuel vehicles running on 85% to 100% ethanol-blended petrol

NEW DELHI: Government on Monday notified a change in Central Motor Vehicles Rules, allowing flex-fuel vehicles that can run on upto 100% ethanol blended petrol. This comes barely months before some of the car manufacturers are set to launch their E100 models.An official said the amendments update the emission provisions by including E100 alongside E85. Officials said E85 and E100 are "intended only for vehicles specially designed and certified to use it and will not be applicable for other vehicles. Vehicles that use E20 or normal fuel can't use E85 or E100 fuel. This notification doesn't require owners of existing vehicles to switch to E85 or modify their vehicles either at present or in future. "Officials said Flex Fuel technology is used in countries such as Brazil and the US. These vehicles are specially designed to operate on a range of ethanol and petrol blends using a single tank fuel. Depending on the vehicle's design and certification, this range may extend to E85 or E100, a fuel predominantly consisting of ethanol.Officials also said that ethanol has lower fossil carbon footprint than conventional petrol and the use of higher ethanol blends can help reduce tailpipe emission of carbon monoxide (CO) and certain hydrocarbons. Greater ethanol use will also reduce dependence on import of crude oil.
Article Summary: Govt allows registration of flex-fuel vehicles running on 85% to 100% ethanol- blended petrol. This comes barely months before some of the car manufacturers are set to launch their E100 models. Vehicles that use E20 or normal fuel can't use E85 or E100 fuel.

Article Title: Meta seeks up to $95bn in equity

Article Title: India-US trade portal sees 3,500 registrations within months of launch, says Piyush Goyal
Article Text:
"This Trade Facilitation Portal is a landmark initiative," said Piyush Goyal

The India-US Trade Facilitation Portal has attracted around 3,500 registrations within months of its launch, commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal said, highlighting its role in helping Indian exporters, particularly MSMEs and first-time exporters, connect with American buyers.In a post on X, Goyal described the response as encouraging and said the initiative was creating new opportunities for businesses in both countries to establish partnerships and expand their presence in international markets. “Trust. Trade. Opportunities. This Trade Facilitation Portal is a landmark initiative seamlessly connecting businesses on both sides,” Goyal said.The portal is a digital business-to-business (B2B) marketplace launched by the Consulate General of India in New York, in collaboration with other Indian consulates in the United States and the Indian Embassy in Washington DC.Designed to facilitate trade between Indian exporters and US buyers, the platform provides a common digital space where businesses can showcase products, identify potential partners and explore commercial opportunities across sectors.It offers category-wise product listings, search tools and personalised dashboards to help users track business leads, monitor trade activity and assess engagement. The platform also hosts virtual exhibitions and curated product showcases, allowing exporters to reach potential buyers without relying solely on physical trade events.The initiative is aimed at simplifying cross-border business interactions and making the US market more accessible to smaller Indian enterprises seeking international customers.Highlighting its potential, Goyal said, “It will open up new opportunities for Indian businesses, particularly MSMEs & first-time exporters, to forge partnerships, explore new markets & expand their global reach.”The registrations mark an early response to the initiative as India seeks to strengthen business-to-business engagement with the United States and widen export opportunities for smaller enterprises.
Article Summary: The India-US Trade Facilitation Portal has attracted around 3,500 registrations within months of its launch. The portal is a digital business-to-business (B2B) marketplace launched by the Consulate General of India in New York, in collaboration with other Indian consulates in the United States.

Article Title: Tata Motor’s Iveco takeover bid clears 80% threshold
Article Text:
File photo: Tata Motors

MUMBAI: Tata Motors’ €3.91 billion (Rs 42,561 crore) acquisition of Italian commercial vehicle maker Iveco has cleared the key acceptance threshold, paving the way for the Indian group to take full ownership of the company and delist the stock from Euronext Milan.The offer secured acceptances representing 87.8% of Iveco’s shares by the close of the tender period on Monday, comfortably exceeding the 80% threshold required for the offer to become effective. The Iveco acquisition is the largest deal under Tata Group chairman N Chandrasekaran.Tata Motors will also acquire Iveco’s 1.8% treasury stock. Treasury shares are a company’s own shares that have been repurchased and held on its balance sheet. They carry no voting rights and, under Dutch rules (although Iveco is listed in Milan, it is governed by Dutch law because it is legally incorporated in the Netherlands), cannot be tendered in the takeover offer. As a result, they are excluded from the acceptance threshold calculation, although their inclusion takes Tata Motors’ total economic interest in Iveco to 89.6%.Having crossed the 80% threshold, Tata Motors can now move to acquire the remaining shares and take Iveco private, with the delisting expected within one to two months.Acceptances had stood at just 35% as of October 22.The offer, which opened on September 4, was sweetened on October 9 when Tata Motors raised its bid to €14.40 a share from €14.10, lifting the maximum deal value to €3.91 billion from €3.8 billion (Rs 41,363 crore) first announced on July 30, 2025.Under the original terms, the offer was conditional on securing 95% of Iveco's share capital, the standard threshold required under Dutch law for a statutory squeeze-out of minority shareholders. Treasury shares were excluded from this calculation.That 95% threshold automatically fell to 80% after Iveco shareholders approved a so-called “back-end” resolution at an extraordinary general meeting on October 16. Under this mechanism, Tata Motors, if it secures 80% of the shares, can merge Iveco with its acquisition vehicle or transfer the company’s assets to it, achieving the same practical outcome as a traditional 95% squeeze-out.Minority shareholders who did not tender their holdings will not retain shares in the listed company. Instead, they will be compelled to accept the same €14.40-a-share cash consideration offered during the tender process. Approval of the back-end resolution was widely seen as a sign of strong institutional support for the deal.
Article Summary: Tata Motors’ €3.91 billion acquisition of Italian commercial vehicle maker Iveco has cleared the key acceptance threshold. Indian group to take full ownership of the company and delist the stock from Euronext Milan. The offer secured acceptances representing 87.8% of Ive co’s shares by the close of the tender period on Monday.

Article Title: Ather reports first profit, approves Rs 122 cr expansion
Article Text:
Bengaluru:

Ather Energy reported its first profit as higher sales, price increases and a shift towards more profitable scooter variants helped it absorb rising raw material costs. The Bengaluru-based company also approved a Rs 122 crore investment to expand production as demand outstrips supply.The electric scooter maker posted a profit of Rs 1.2 crore for the September quarter, compared with a loss of Rs 154 crore a year earlier and Rs 51 crore in the preceding quarter. Total income rose 62% year-on-year to Rs 1,527 crore, while vehicle sales increased 42% to 93,211 units.“We’re not out of the woods,” co-founder and CEO Tarun Mehta told analysts. He said the focus remained on increasing sales and production, cautioning that quarterly profits could fluctuate.Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) stood at Rs 74.2 crore, compared with a loss of Rs 90.8 crore a year earlier. The company’s earnings included Rs 62.7 crore in other income.Price increases and changes in the mix of variants sold helped offset higher costs of aluminium, copper, battery materials and plastics.However, Mehta said some margin gains from prioritising certain variants and reducing incentives were more temporary.“On the current portfolio, I would not want to push pricing up, at least over the next few quarters,” he said.The company said pre-orders more than doubled to about 1.8 lakh during the quarter. Mehta estimated that its existing stores could sell roughly 20,000 additional scooters a month if supplies were available. Its Hosur factory operated at 98% capacity utilisation during peak production.The expansion will increase Hosur’s annual vehicle capacity from 4.2 lakh to 4.95 lakh units by December. Ather’s new factory at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar in Maharashtra is scheduled to begin commercial production in phases from December, initially with an annual capacity of five lakh units.The additional investment will raise the new factory’s planned capacity to 6.5 lakh units by the September quarter of 2027, taking combined annual capacity to about 11.4 lakh units. Mehta said installed capacity would take additional time to ramp up fully.Supply constraints have also shaped the rollout of Ather’s new Konarc scooter. The company prioritised mid-range versions over the entry-level variant to protect margins while production remained constrained. The cheaper version will follow as additional capacity becomes available.
Article Summary: Ather Energy reported its first profit as higher sales, price increases and a shift towards more profitable scooter variants helped it absorb rising raw material costs. Total income rose 62% year-on-year to Rs 1,527 crore, while vehicle sales increased 42% to 93,211 units.

Article Title: NHAI sets 3-month deadline to improve ‘look and feel’ of national highways
Article Text:
NHAI identifies 25-plus measures to fix road defects, improve highway safety, cleanliness and infrastructure across India over the next three months

NEW DELHI: National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has identified over two dozen items for improvement over the next three months to enhance “look and feel” of national highways and improve commuters' experience. The exercise will focus on rectifying road defects, improving safety features, maintaining cleanliness and upgrading highway infrastructure.TOI has learnt that the authority has asked all its regional officers, project directors and highway contractors to focus on these areas. The identified measures include filling potholes, repairing cracked road surfaces, addressing visible rutting, restoring faded pavement markings and fixing damaged kerbs. NHAI has also flagged defunct highway lighting, damaged road signs and overhead sign structures, broken concrete barriers and faded paintwork for rectification.The authority will use dashcam footage to identify defects that need to be fixed. Other priorities include dressing uneven earthen shoulders, removing vegetation, ensuring proper median plantation, replacing missing drain covers and closing unauthorised openings in road medians.Unauthorised signboards, hoardings and encroachments will also be addressed.Work-zone safety and proper arrangements for traffic diversions are among the items identified for immediate attention.In addition, NHAI has proposed providing an adequate number of road studs, installing impact attenuators (crash cushions) at hazardous locations and adding gantries where required. The plan also covers improving the quality of toilets, painting foot overbridges and gantries, refurbishing bus bays and deploying road-sweeping and drain-cleaning machines.The authority has also identified toll plaza approaches, service roads, waterlogging, highway slopes and approaches to structures for improvement. Measures include better signage, road markings and landscaping near toll plazas, smoother riding surfaces and preventing water ponding.
Article Summary: National Highways Authority of India has identified over two dozen items for improvement over the next three months. The exercise will focus on rectifying road defects, improving safety features, maintaining cleanliness and upgrading highway infrastructure. Measures include filling potholes, repairing cracked road surfaces, addressing visible rutting and restoring faded pavement markings.

Article Title: Piyush Goyal holds talks with global tech and manufacturing firms on India investment opportunities
Article Text:
Piyush Goyal with Juvencio Maeztu, CEO & President of Ingka Group (IKEA)

Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has held discussions with executives of semiconductor equipment maker ASML, chipmaker Nexperia, IKEA operator Ingka Group and clean-energy company Power2X, as India seeks to attract investment and expand cooperation with European businesses in technology, manufacturing and renewable energy.The meetings took place during Goyal’s visit to the Netherlands, which included the India-Netherlands Business Forum in The Hague on Monday. The minister used the forum to pitch India as an investment destination, highlighting its growing consumer market, manufacturing capabilities and opportunities in emerging industries.In a post on X, Goyal said his meeting with Wayne Allan, executive vice-president and member of ASML’s board of management, focused on advanced semiconductor technologies, innovation and skill development. “With a strong policy push in India, growing investments, and an expanding talent pool, we explored avenues for collaboration in cutting-edge semiconductor technologies, innovation, and skilling to strengthen India's position in the global chip value chain,” Goyal said.Discussions with Stefan Tilgner, interim CEO of Nexperia, centred on expanding semiconductor cooperation. Goyal said India’s growing electronics manufacturing capabilities and technology ecosystem offered opportunities to strengthen partnerships and build more resilient supply chains.Goyal also met Juvencio Maeztu, CEO and president of Ingka Group, which operates IKEA, to discuss manufacturing and sourcing opportunities. “Discussed opportunities offered by our growing consumer market & how IKEA can leverage India's manufacturing capabilities to strengthen its global sourcing network,” he said.The minister’s meeting with Occo Roelofsen, founder and CEO of Power2X, focused on India-Netherlands cooperation in green hydrogen, renewable energy and emerging technologies.Addiitonally, at the India-Netherlands Business Forum, Goyal called on European businesses to deepen their engagement with India and argued that companies needed fewer regulatory hurdles and simpler procedures. “The world wants deregulation. The world wants more freedom. The business world is looking for less compliance burden, simpler processes, simpler procedures, less paperwork,” he said.Goyal also highlighted the investment potential of India’s expanding power capacity and growing clean-energy base, particularly for data centres and other energy-intensive industries. He said the sector could attract around $200 billion in investments over the coming years.His remarks came amid a broader debate over the European Union’s regulatory framework and its Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM). Dutch mMinister for foreign trade and development cooperation Sjoerd Sjoerdsma defended regulations covering climate, product quality and safety, while saying rules that unnecessarily hinder trade should be reviewed.
Article Summary: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal held discussions with executives of semiconductor equipment maker ASML, chipmaker Nexperia, IKEA operator Ingka Group and clean-energy company Power2X. Goyal said India’s growing electronics manufacturing capabilities and technology ecosystem offered opportunities to strengthen partnerships.

Article Title: WTW executives sacking was wrongful, rules court in Bengaluru
Article Text:
Bengaluru court rules WTW executive's termination wrongful, awards Rs 3.6 crore in damages and Rs 10 lakh for mental agony.

BENGALURU: A Bengaluru court has ruled that the termination of former Willis Towers Watson (WTW) executive Naveen Kumar Midha was wrongful and unlawful, awarding him Rs 3.6 crore in damages and Rs 10 lakh for mental agony, anguish and harassment. The LXIX Additional City Civil and Sessions Court also directed WTW-related entities to issue Midha a fresh, professionally worded relieving letter and remove adverse remarks about his conduct and integrity from his employment records.Midha had alleged that he was dismissed in September 2018 after raising concerns about financial irregularities and unethical practices at the company. He also accused senior executives of making defamatory statements that damaged his professional reputation. The court partly decreed his suit, holding that the termination by Willis Towers Watson India Insurance Brokers was wrongful.It directed four corporate defendants — the Indian insurance broking company, Willis Europe, Willis Towers Watson and Willis Towers Watson India — to jointly pay Rs 3.6 crore in special damages within 30 days. The court also awarded Rs 10 lakh in compensation for mental agony and harassment.
Article Summary: Naveen Kumar Midha had alleged that he was dismissed in September 2018. Midha accused senior executives of making defamatory statements. The court partly decreed his suit, holding that the termination by Willis Towers Watson India Insurance Brokers was wrongful.

Article Title: Blackstone’s GCC in Bengaluru anchors fresh $50 billion India plan
Article Text:
First Centre Outside US As Firm Targets $100 Billion India Investments By 2030

Bengaluru:

Blackstone has launched a global capability centre (GCC) in Bengaluru, its first outside the US, underscoring India’s growing importance to the investment firm’s global operations. The move comes as the firm looks to double its investments in India to $100 billion over the next five years from about $51 billion invested to date.Blackstone vice-chairman and CFO Michael Chae said the Bengaluru team would be closely integrated with the firm’s global operations and support functions spanning finance, technology, human resources, legal and compliance.“We have about 170 employees in India, of whom around 90 are in Mumbai, our headquarters. We have been running our investment operations in Mumbai very successfully for two decades now. Bengaluru currently has about 80 employees, and that team will grow, as will our Mumbai team. They will work closely with our teams around the world to help drive our operations globally,” Chae said.The centre is not intended to function as a standalone unit. Its expansion reflects the firm’s growing operational needs as Blackstone’s assets under management have quadrupled over the past decade to nearly $1.4 trillion.The Bengaluru GCC is led by Susan Yung, senior managing director in credit and insurance investment operations. Yung previously worked in India and was managing director at Goldman Sachs’ captive centre in Bengaluru. Blackstone has also hired senior leaders across key functions, including engineering, whose team will work with the firm’s global chief technology officer.The Bengaluru team is expected to grow to 100 or more employees by the end of the year, Chae said.Blackstone’s biggest investments in India include Mphasis, Federal Bank and commercial property. The company is said to be India’s largest institutional commercial real estate owner, with $22 billion in assets and control over more than 150 million sq ft of office and retail space. These properties cater particularly to technology companies, including other GCCs. Blackstone-backed companies have been involved in five of India’s six real estate investment trusts (REITs), including Embassy REIT.On AI’s potential impact on jobs and office demand, Chae said it was too early to conclude that the technology would lead to widespread job losses. “We don’t see AI as some existential negative for IT services companies. Like most businesses, there’s an opportunity to get ahead of the risk of disruption and enable their own tools and services,” he said, noting that predictions of a “job apocalypse” had not materialised.Chae cited Mphasis as an example of a company using AI to strengthen its business. He said Blackstone continued to assess service providers on the capabilities they could bring to its portfolio companies.Many businesses, he said, would continue to rely on IT services partners rather than build all their AI capabilities in-house, given the investment and time required.Blackstone’s other investment themes include travel and leisure, including luxury hotels; technology and AI infrastructure, including Neysa and AirTrunk; and manufacturing and e-commerce. Its logistics platform, Horizon Industrial Parks, has scaled up to become India’s largest logistics park platform.
Article Summary: Blackstone has launched a global capability centre (GCC) in Bengaluru, its first outside the US. The move comes as the firm looks to double its investments in India to $100 billion over the next five years. The Bengaluru GCC is led by Susan Yung, senior managing director in credit and insurance investment operations.

Article Title: FDI inflows up 68% in Aug, seen topping $100bn in FY27
Article Text:
File photo: Foreign direct investment

NEW DELHI: Foreign direct investment has made a strong comeback with inflows rising 67.7% to $11 billion in Aug, while net inflows - after factoring in outward FDI and remittances - were pegged at $3.3 billion as against net outflows of $103 million in Aug 2025.Based on the current trend of over $55 billion FDI inflows, on a gross basis, during April-Aug, govt officials are confident of India topping the $100-billion mark during the current financial year, a first for the country. Net inflows during the first five months of the fiscal were estimated at $19 billion during April-Aug, 68% higher than a year ago, according to the latest data released by the Reserve Bank of India. During April-Sept 2026, FDI flows in China (based on actual use) added up to Yuan 548.8 billion ($82.2 billion), which was a decline of 4.3%, according to a Chinese media report.In India, FDI through the equity investment route shot up 87.5% during the month to nearly $7.5 billion, while reinvested earnings were flat at just under $2.2 billion. On the outflows side, repatriation was also 26% higher at $5.8 billion. There was an 11% fall in outward FDI to $1.9 billion, according to the latest data.Govt has been seeking to boost FDI inflows and has been less bothered about outward FDI with policymakers arguing that it also reflects the growing global footprint of Indian companies, which are seeking to be part of the global value chain.A large part of the FDI intentions announced are related to data centres, some of which have started flowing. While latest disaggregated data is unavailable, during the first quarter, services accounted for 36% of the inflows, followed by 14% in computer hardware and software.
Article Summary: Foreign direct investment has made a strong comeback with inflows rising 67.7% to $11 billion in Aug. Based on the current trend of over $55 billion FDI inflows, on a gross basis, during April-Aug, govt officials are confident of India topping the $100-billion mark during the current financial year.

Article Title: Expect rates to increase by 50bps in Dec: SBI chief
Article Text:
File photo: SBI chairman CS Setty during a press conference in Mumbai

MUMBAI: State Bank of India expects interest rates to rise by 50 basis points in Dec, with chairman C S Setty saying higher rates could affect discretionary consumption credit demand but were unlikely to significantly dent overall credit growth given a 7.1% growth forecast for the economy."Interest rates will influence the composition and quantum of credit demand, not immediately," Setty said at the Business Standard BFSI Summit. "We need to distinguish between weakening of demand and moderation of credit growth. We are coming from a phase of robust growth in credit. While discretionary consumption demand could be affected, I do not think credit for productive activities will be impacted," he said.Setty said he did not expect system-wide concerns over credit quality, although individual borrowers could face stress from higher interest rates.On deposits, Setty said household savings were undergoing a structural shift, with households increasingly practising asset allocation, even if they were not fully conscious of it. "There is only so much that rates can propel you in deposit mobilisation. What matters is service quality," he said, adding that the ease of moving funds from savings accounts to term deposits had improved significantly."The liquidity RBI has been providing and the FCNR flows will ensure that there is no rate-driven competition for deposits," he said, adding that market movements could trigger some shifts in household savings.
Article Summary: State Bank of India expects interest rates to rise by 50 basis points in Dec. Chairman C S Setty said higher rates could affect discretionary consumption credit demand. But he said they were unlikely to significantly dent overall credit growth given a 7.1% growth forecast for the economy.

Article Title: 'Shooters fired at actor Tiger Shroff on 3rd attempt, did recce of other actors including Salman, Aamir': Mumbai Police
Article Text:
Three shooters were allegedly targeting actor Tiger Shroff and had previously scouted other Bollywood celebrities





MUMBAI: The October 18 firing at actor Tiger Shroff was allegedly the third attempt by the shooters to target him, with the accused claiming during interrogation that they had conducted reconnaissance of several Bollywood actors before zeroing in on Shroff, police sources said.According to sources, the three shooters, Phool Singh, 19, Rehan Ansari, 19, and Rithik Mahato, 22, told investigators that in the first week of October, they allegedly received instructions from Lawrence Bishnoi gangster Anil Pandit to identify potential targets, including actors Salman Khan, Aamir Khan, Akshay Kumar and Amitabh Bachchan.The accused allegedly recced these actors but failed to locate them or found it difficult to get close to them. Pandit subsequently, through voice notes, instructed them to target Tiger Shroff, son of actor Jackie Shroff.During the second week of October, the accused allegedly learnt that Tiger regularly worked out at MMV Matrix Gym, owned by his family, on Linking Road in Khar.The shooters reportedly spotted the actor outside the gym on one occasion but were not prepared to carry out the attack.“They decided to return the next day at the same time, but Tiger did not turn up.They then asked an auto-rickshaw driver where they could get to see filmstars. The driver allegedly told them that they could spot Tiger Shroff at a ground near Pushpa Park in Juhu where he regularly comes to play football,” a source said.Acting on this information, the shooters allegedly lay in wait at the ground on October 11, but Tiger did not arrive. They subsequently returned on October 18, allegedly armed and prepared to execute the attack.The firing left Tiger’s driver and a vlogger injured, while the actor escaped with minor injuries. The police are now looking for the auto-rickshaw driver so that they can make him a witness in the case.
Article Summary: The October 18 firing at actor Tiger Shroff was allegedly the third attempt by the shooters to target him. The three shooters, Phool Singh, Rehan Ansari, and Rithik Mahato, told investigators that in the first week of October, they allegedly received instructions from gangster Anil Pandit.

Article Title: Instagram tests 90-minute horizontal videos - what it means for long-form content creators
Article Text:
Instagram is also experimenting with “Series”, a feature that gives episodic Reels a dedicated space on a creator’s profile (Photo: AP).

Instagram on Monday began testing new features, including 90-minute horizontal videos to target long-form content creators like podcasters and comedians, with select creators in the US.The feature, called “Features”, will allow them to link short reel clips, typically around three minutes or less, to full-length videos, as per The Hollywood Reporter.“What you’re now going to be able to do is, you see a clip of a podcast that you love, you can just click and continue watching or watch the full video, and you’ll be able to dive in and see the whole thing because creators are going to be able to link these Reels to their overall feature,” vice-president of product at Instagram, Tessa Lyons, said.Instagram has already been testing Features with creators in Brazil and plans to expand the trial to tens of thousands of creators in the US. The videos will reportedly be recommended to users through the Explore page and other areas of the platform.The feature will be available on mobile, with Instagram aiming to extend the viewing experience to its TV app. Instagram for TV, which launched last year and is available on Samsung , Fire TV and Google TV, is now expanding to Apple TV in the US.“We think the best viewing experience for longform horizontal content is on a big, horizontal screen, and so I think that is where we will expect a lot of the deep consumption to happen over time,” Lyons said, as per The Hollywood Reporter.Instagram is also experimenting with “Series”, a feature that gives episodic Reels a dedicated space on a creator’s profile. The move comes amid growing interest in microdramas and episodic videos among creators.In June, the company began reaching out to microdrama studios in Southeast Asia to test the feature. It has since approached individual creators who have been experimenting with episodic content.Instagram plans to begin testing Series in more countries in the coming months, with a US launch targeted for the end of this year or early next year. The company has also started testing how the feature will appear on television.Other experiments include integrating live videos into the Reels tab and recommending them to users who do not follow the creators. The test is launching in Indonesia and Brazil, with an expansion to the US planned for next year.
Article Summary: Instagram on Monday began testing new features, including 90-minute horizontal videos to target long-form content creators like podcasters and comedians. The feature, called “Features”, will allow them to link short reel clips, typically around three minutes or less, to full-length videos. The videos will reportedly be recommended to users through the Explore page and other areas of the platform.

Article Title: Anthropic files IPO, could be biggest ever
Article Text:
Anthropic is gearing up for its IPO, aiming to go public on the Nasdaq

Artificial intelligence giant Anthropic filed papers Monday for what could be the biggest initial public offering of stock ever even as its top executive warns that advanced AI could pose an existential threat to humanity.The filing sets up the San Francisco company for a Wall Street debut next month, potentially eclipsing SpaceX IPO in June that raised a record $86 billion. An Anthropic IPO would also put the company ahead of OpenAI in going public in what is expected to be a pair of blockbuster stock debuts for the rival AI labs.The filing comes weeks after CEO Dario Amodei argued in an essay for slowing the development of the most advanced AI models. An IPO could provide Anthropic with enormous resources to accelerate its expansion. The amount the company ultimately raises remains uncertain, as do its final valuation and offering price, but even at lower estimates, it would turn the five-year-old startup into one of the world’s most valuable companies and potentially boost the wealth of Amodei and his sister and co-founder, Daniela, by billions of dollars.The 335-page document showed Anthropic’s revenue is growing rapidly, but like many other tech companies going public, it has yet to turn a profit. The company behind the chatbot Claude reported a net loss of $80.7 billion in the first half of 2026. That compares to a loss of $13 billion in the same period a year earlier.Despite the losses, Anthropic, valued earlier this year at $965 billion by private investors, is reportedly set to see that value rise to $1.5 trillion or possibly $2 trillion, although its final valuation has not been established. At $1.5 trillion, Anthropic would rank among the world’s most valuable public companies, alongside Tesla.As for money raised, the offering could bring in as much as $100 billion, according to reports, surpassing the current record set by another one of Musk’s companies, SpaceX, earlier this year. Anthropic, meanwhile, emphasised the potential for its AI to “behave in unintended, misaligned, or autonomous ways” in the filing. If its technologies are not developed with adequate safeguards and oversight, it could “pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity, particularly if such systems were misused, replicated, weaponized, or allowed to operate with a high degree of autonomy. ”
Article Summary: Anthropic filed papers for what could be the biggest initial public offering of stock ever even as its top executive warns that advanced AI could pose an existential threat to humanity. The filing sets up the San Francisco company for a Wall Street debut next month, potentially eclipsing SpaceX IPO in June that raised a record $86 billion.

Article Title: Middle East conflict may end, but energy crisis will drag on: IEA chief explains
Article Text:
IEA's Birol does not expect energy markets to return to pre-war levels in 2027

Oil prices near $120 a barrel add to economic pressure

Winter demand and refinery maintenance threaten fuel supplies

Europe faces a difficult winter

With oil prices edging towards $120 a barrel and winter adding to concerns over fuel supplies, the global energy crisis could outlast the Iran war itself.International Energy Agency (IEA) executive director Fatih Birol has warned that energy markets are unlikely to return to their pre-war conditions in 2027, urging governments and businesses to put energy security first.Speaking at the Singapore International Energy Week conference on Monday, Birol said that the conflict, which began in late February, had upended expectations of a surplus in the energy market this year. Instead, disruptions to global energy flows have tightened supplies and pushed up oil benchmarks and refined fuel prices."I am afraid I don't see any credible pathway that the markets will go next year, where we were before this war has started," Birol said.He called on countries and companies to prepare for a prolonged period of uncertainty, with energy security taking priority while they also consider what comes next."So therefore, we all need to get prepared, taking the energy security as a number one priority in our government, business world, but without forgetting what is the next chapter for the countries and for companies that are all here today," he said.The pressure on oil markets has already been visible in prices.More Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia sent Brent crude futures soaring to $117 a barrel on Friday, their highest level in nearly six months. Prices eased to $115 per barrel on Monday but still remained about 59% above their pre-war level."Oil prices are flirting with $120 a barrel and the prices for products are even much higher," Birol said.While he declined to predict where oil prices would go next, he warned that costs at these levels were becoming a major burden for several economies."I can tell you that the current price of oil is, for some countries, for example in Europe, maybe not so high and affordable. But in many parts of the world, having almost $120 oil prices is having a major impact on trade deficits."Oil is not the only concern. As winter approaches, Birol is also worried about the availability and cost of refined products, particularly diesel, which is used for heating in parts of the West.Demand for diesel typically rises during the colder months, just as several refineries are scheduled to undergo maintenance, adding another pressure point for fuel markets."I am worried on top of that for refined products because we are entering...winter season. Some parts of the world, where typically diesel demand goes high and several refineries are going through maintenance period."Europe, meanwhile, faces a difficult winter on the gas front. Countries have decided to cut imports of Russian gas, while the Iran war has added to the strain by disrupting gas exports from Qatar and the United Arab Emirates."In Europe, we are facing a tough winter because European countries have decided to cut gas imports from Russia and with the additional problem now rising from the Iran war, namely Qatar and the Emirates not being able to export gas as they were before, will put significant pressure on gas markets."The energy crisis could also give nuclear power a fresh push. Birol expects a "strong comeback" for the sector as countries grapple with the current situation. The IEA's recent survey found that 90 gigawatts of nuclear power capacity was under construction, the highest level in the past four decades, he said.
Article Summary: IEA executive director Fatih Birol warns energy markets are unlikely to return to pre-war conditions in 2027. He urges governments and businesses to put energy security first. Winter demand and refinery maintenance threaten fuel supplies in Europe and the U.S.

Article Title: Crude prices fall from six-month highs; WTI stands at $101 per barrel, Brent costs $115
Article Text:
Crude prcies fall from six month-highs, but trade beyond $100 per barrel

Strait of Hormuz remains a key concern

Supply measures fail to reverse the rally

Oil prices fell over 1% on Monday after surging to near six-month highs late last week. Despite the decline, prices remained elevated, with Brent crude hovering near $115 per barrel as continued attacks on Saudi Arabia kept concerns over global oil supplies alive.The US Federal Reserve's upcoming policy decision is another factor investors will watch as crude enters a potentially volatile week.WTI crude fell 1.71%, or $1.77, to $101.5 per barrel, while Brent crude declined 1.41%, or $1.65, to $115.1 per barrel.The decline followed a sharp rise on Friday, when prices settled nearly $3 higher after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia raised concerns about energy supplies. Brent recorded a 6% gain for the week, while WTI advanced 2.3%, taking prices close to six-month highs.The security situation remained tense over the weekend. The Houthis said they had attacked a Saudi airport and oil facilities on Saturday, while Saudi Arabia reported intercepting additional missiles and drones on Sunday. The country's main airport resumed partial operations the same day, following damage from an earlier round of Houthi attacks. The militant group has vowed to continue targeting the facility.Developments around the Strait of Hormuz and the security of energy infrastructure are expected to influence crude prices in the coming days. Brent has already crossed $117 per barrel, and analysts said any disruption to energy facilities or shipping through the strait could push global prices towards $120 per barrel. A credible move towards de-escalation, however, could lead to a sharp correction."The near-term bias remains bullish but highly headline-driven; traders should avoid chasing sharp rallies and monitor geopolitical developments, Fed guidance and weekly inventory data for directional confirmation," said Ajit Mishra, SVP - Research at Religare Broking.The latest price rally has been driven by escalating US-Iran tensions, fears of renewed military action, attacks on Saudi infrastructure and threats to important shipping routes, Mishra said. These developments have sustained the geopolitical risk premium in oil prices.Navneet Damani, head of research - commodities at Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd, said, "The rally gathered pace as attention returned to escalating attacks around the Hormuz and Saudi Arabia, reviving concerns over energy infrastructure and export security."Further uncertainty has emerged from reports that the US and Israel had prepared plans to target Iranian energy infrastructure, including nuclear facilities near Natanz, after the US mid-term elections on November 3. Iran warned of repercussions if Washington and Tel Aviv launched an attack, adding to concerns in the market.Efforts to ease supply concerns have so far done little to bring prices down. The International Energy Agency has indicated its readiness to release more strategic stocks, while the G7's additional 100 million barrels largely involves accelerating an existing release programme. The first Russian diesel cargo bound for the US has also failed to reverse the upward trend.According to Damani, market participants are now looking for evidence that these measures will translate into meaningful additional supplies, rather than responding to announcements alone."Although crude flows through Hormuz have shown some recovery, elevated freight costs, constrained regional shipments and persistent security threats continue to undermine export reliability. With physical supply yet to normalise, the risk premium remains elevated, and the balance of risks continues to favour the upside, though credible progress towards de-escalation could still trigger sharp profit-taking," Damani added.The market will also track weekly US inventory estimates from the American Petroleum Institute and the US Energy Information Administration, alongside Cushing crude inventories. These figures could offer further direction as traders assess the state of supply.
Article Summary: WTI crude fell 1.71%, or $1.77, to $101.5 per barrel, while Brent crude declined 1.41% to $115.1 per barrel. The decline followed a sharp rise on Friday, when prices settled nearly $3 higher after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia raised concerns about energy supplies.

Article Title: France’s economic woes: Debt nears 122% of GDP, growth forecast at just 0.4%
Article Text:
France’s debt, taxes and borrowing costs rise as economic growth slows

France’s public debt nears 122% of GDP

Government spending accounts for 57.2% of GDP

France faces higher borrowing costs

France’s growth forecast falls to 0.4%

France is facing mounting pressure on two fronts: growing public anger over the cost of living and an economy struggling with high debt, taxes and weak growth. Student protests that began with school blockades have spread, turning violent, putting the spotlight on the country’s economic troubles and deepening political tensions.The rising cost of living is one of the concerns behind the demonstrations, which began largely peacefully but disrupted schools before escalating into wider unrest and pockets of violence involving young people on Saturday. The issue is not unique to France, but it comes at a difficult time for the country’s economy.France is also struggling to bring its public finances under control. Carsten Brzeski, global chief of macro at ING bank, said “France is not Greece”, referring to the financial crisis that shook the European Union in 2009. However, France has repeatedly failed to meet its targets for spending, economic growth and cost-cutting.With President Emmanuel Macron nearing the end of his nearly decade-long tenure, the state of the country’s finances is also expected to be a key issue in the race to succeed him next spring.France’s public debt stood at nearly 3.6 trillion euros (nearly $4.08 trillion) at the end of June, equivalent to 119% of its gross domestic product (GDP).The government has warned that the figure could rise further. Three weeks ago, it said the budget would again exceed European Union spending limits, with public debt expected to reach nearly 122% of GDP, setting a new record, AP reported.The growing debt leaves the government with difficult choices. It needs to reduce spending or raise taxes, which are already among the highest in Europe.Gilbert Cette, an economics professor at Neoma Business School in Paris, described the debt as “enormous”, saying, “France’s entire economic policy is constrained by such a sizable debt level.”Cette said France had shown “talent” in both increasing government spending and cutting taxes in recent years, making it harder to get public finances back on track.Brzeski also warned that France’s approach to economic reforms was affecting its credibility. Writing last week, he said, “Greece’s credibility was destroyed by false statistics; France’s is being eroded by false promises and the inability or unwillingness to start fiscal and structural reforms,”High government spending is another challenge for France. In 2025, public expenditure accounted for 57.2% of the country’s economic output, according to Eurostat, the European Union’s statistics agency. The EU average was just under 50%.A large share of this spending goes towards healthcare, pensions and subsidies for businesses. With government expenditure already making up such a large part of the economy, reducing it further would require difficult decisions.France also has one of the highest tax burdens in the European Union. Tax revenue and social contributions accounted for 45.2% of GDP in 2024, putting the country a close second behind Denmark, according to Eurostat. The EU average was just over 40%.This leaves the government with limited room to raise taxes further to reduce the deficit. Cutting spending is another option, but it would mean making choices about areas that already account for a significant share of the economy.The cost of borrowing is adding to the pressure on France’s public finances. The yield on its 10-year government bond stood at 4.96% as of Tuesday.Higher bond yields mean the government has to pay more to borrow money. This can leave less room in the budget for other priorities, including pensions, education, healthcare, defence and social programmes.Germany, the European Union’s largest economy, faces lower borrowing costs. Its equivalent 10-year government bond, known as the Bund, had a yield of about 3.4%.The gap between French and German 10-year bond yields has widened, highlighting the difference in borrowing costs between the two countries. This adds to the challenges facing France as it tries to manage its debt and spending.France’s economic outlook remains weak. The International Monetary Fund has forecast growth of just 0.4% for the country this year, the lowest rate among developed economies.The forecast is well below the expected growth rates for both the global economy and advanced economies. Global output is projected to grow by 3.1% this year, while advanced economies are expected to expand by 2.1%.France’s projected growth is around one-third of Germany’s forecast rate and half of Italy’s. Japan, which has the second-lowest growth forecast among developed countries, is expected to grow by 0.7%.Slow growth makes it harder for France to manage its public finances while dealing with high debt, substantial government spending and an already heavy tax burden. Rising borrowing costs further add to the pressure.With the economy growing slowly and public finances under strain, France faces difficult choices over how to control its debt and spending. These economic challenges are unfolding alongside political divisions and protests over the cost of living, while the state of public finances is set to remain an important issue ahead of next spring’s presidential succession race.
Article Summary: France’s public debt stood at nearly 3.6 trillion euros (nearly $4.08 trillion) at the end of June, equivalent to 119% of its gross domestic product (GDP) The government has warned that the figure could rise further, with public debt expected to reach nearly 122% of GDP. High government spending is another challenge for France. In 2025, public expenditure accounted for 57.2% of the country's economic output, according to Eurostat.

Article Title: US Fed expected to hold rates as inflation, energy costs weigh ahead of midterms
Article Text:
US Fed expected to hold interest rates steady despite persistent inflation (representative image)

Inflation pressures complicate Fed's rate decision

Former Fed official says economic data favour further hikes

Trump's criticism of Fed independence

The US Federal Reserve is widely expected to keep interest rates unchanged at its meeting next week, despite persistent inflation and market expectations of at least one more rate hike before the end of the year, according to analysts cited by news agency AFP.The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) will meet over two days, with its interest rate decision scheduled for 2 pm local time (1800 GMT) on Wednesday.At its September meeting, the Fed raised its benchmark federal funds rate for the first time in three years, taking the target range to 3.75%-4%. The central bank has struggled to bring inflation down to its long-term target of 2%, which it has missed for more than five years.The decision comes just days before the November 3 US midterm elections, in which Democrats are seeking to wrest control of both chambers of Congress from President Donald Trump's Republican Party.The Fed's preferred inflation gauge, the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, reached a pandemic-era peak of 7.2% in 2022 before a series of interest rate increases brought it down to around 2.2% by late 2024.However, inflation subsequently rose again amid Trump's economic policies, including tariffs that disrupted global trade and the US war with Iran. The PCE index reached a three-year high of 3.9% in May.Since the US and Israel attacked Iran in late February, global energy prices have surged, with retaliatory actions by Tehran sharply restricting oil and gas supplies through the Gulf. Higher energy costs have also begun feeding into the prices of other goods and services, putting affordability at the forefront of concerns ahead of the midterm elections.The Fed faces the challenge of controlling inflation while supporting the labour market. Higher interest rates increase borrowing costs, potentially slowing economic activity and curbing price pressures, but they can also weigh on employment.The US economy has also been dealing with weakening consumer confidence and signs of stress in an otherwise resilient jobs market. The latest consumer confidence survey from the Conference Board was expected to show a further decline in October after confidence fell in September to its lowest level in more than a decade.Loretta Mester, a former president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland, told AFP that the timing of the meeting ahead of the elections would not influence policymakers' decision."The Fed doesn't take into account any kind of political issues in that FOMC room," she said. "It really is based on the economics."Mester argued that economic conditions supported further monetary tightening, pointing to a stable labour market and inflation remaining above the central bank's target."The data that's come in continue to show a stable labor market and continue to show inflation above target," she said, adding that there was no evidence of inflation moving towards the target."The economics would suggest then you need to continue raising rates."However, Mester said most policymakers appeared reluctant to move too quickly. She expected the Fed could hold rates steady in October and consider another increase at its next meeting in early December.Wendy Edelberg, a senior fellow at the Brookings Institution, also said that central bankers would prefer to avoid becoming part of the political debate ahead of the elections."It's unhelpful for everyone if the Fed gets wrapped up in all the political discourse right before an election," she said.Edelberg added that raising rates in December rather than October would have limited economic implications.She viewed a possible delay less as a concession to Trump, who has repeatedly called for lower interest rates, and more as a way for the Fed to avoid becoming a target of political criticism.Trump has repeatedly criticised the Federal Reserve over interest rates, which he considers too high. However, he has so far refrained from directing similar criticism at Kevin Warsh, whom he appointed to succeed Jerome Powell as Fed chair.Since returning to power last year, Trump has mounted an unprecedented challenge to the central bank's independence. His administration launched a criminal investigation into Powell and attempted to remove Fed Governor Lisa Cook.The investigation into Powell was dropped to smooth the way for Warsh's confirmation by the Senate, while the legal battle over Cook's removal continued despite a Supreme Court decision nullifying an earlier attempt to dismiss her.Last week, Cook declined to attend a hearing in a White House investigation into mortgage fraud allegations, which she denies.Meanwhile, the Fed's rate decision will come during a busy week for US economic data.Investors and policymakers were also awaiting updates on inflation, consumer confidence and third-quarter economic growth, alongside earnings reports from major companies.
Article Summary: US Federal Reserve is widely expected to keep interest rates unchanged at its meeting next week. The central bank has struggled to bring inflation down to its long-term target of 2%. The decision comes just days before the November 3 US midterm elections, in which Democrats are seeking to wrest control of both chambers of Congress.

Article Title: From fuel price hikes to cost-of-living concerns, US consumer sentiment nears record low
Article Text:
File photo: A shopper looks at the section of a grocery store in Fort Worth, Texas (Picture credit: AP)

Independent voters report weaker sentiment

Inflation expectations remain elevated

Federal Reserve decision due next week

US consumer sentiment edged down to near a record low in October as rising prices linked to the Middle East conflict weighed on households' views of the economy, a University of Michigan survey showed on Friday, with affordability emerging as a key issue ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.The university's Consumer Sentiment Index slipped to 48.0 this month from a final reading of 48.1 in September.Economists polled by Reuters had expected a reading of 46.3, which was also the preliminary estimate for October.October's reading was the second-lowest on record, following the all-time low of 44.8 recorded in May, shortly after the Iran war began."Purchasing power continues to dominate consumer views of the economy," said Joanne Hsu, director of the Surveys of Consumers. "Sentiment is now 10% below a year ago and 15% less than February, just prior to the Iran conflict."The survey's findings coincided with political polling showing that voters held a dim view of the economy and President Donald Trump's and the Republican Party's handling of it, Reuters reported.Millions of Americans have already cast early ballots ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, which will determine control of Congress for the final two years of Trump's term.Polls indicated Republicans were likely to lose control of the House of Representatives, with the Senate also potentially at stake. Trump's approval rating in a Reuters/Ipsos poll stood at a record low, amid a surge in fuel prices following his decision to attack Iran in late February.The University of Michigan survey found that the decline in sentiment was driven by respondents who identified as independents, a group that includes swing voters.Their sentiment score fell to 42.4 in October from 47.7 in September, putting it just above May's record low of 40.6. Sentiment scores among Democrats and Republicans improved.The survey also found that more independents and Republicans were citing high prices as a strain on their personal finances. Since January, the number of independents reporting inflation pressures as a financial burden had risen by 27%, while the figure among Republicans had increased by 52%. Among Democrats, the increase was 15%.Households with little or no exposure to the stock market had also increasingly cited high prices as a financial burden compared with the beginning of the year. The stock market had recently climbed rapidly amid enthusiasm for investments in artificial intelligence.The survey's measure of consumers' expectations for inflation over the next 12 months rose to 4.7% in October from 4.6% in September. The measure had stood at 3.4% in February, before the US-Israeli war with Iran began.Expectations for inflation over the next five years increased to 3.5% from 3.4% in September and 3.2% in March, shortly after the conflict began.In an accompanying report, Hsu said persistently elevated inflation expectations in the period following the Covid-19 pandemic posed a risk to the Federal Reserve's efforts to bring inflation down to its 2% target. The target had remained unmet for more than five years, she wrote."Consumers broadly expect inflation to accelerate, and this year’s increases in inflation expectations are not limited to one part of the political spectrum," Hsu said.She also cautioned that relatively resilient consumer spending, despite negative views of the economy, required close attention. If households were spending now to avoid expected price increases in the future, bringing inflation down could become more difficult, she added.Federal Reserve officials are scheduled to meet in Washington next week. Despite recent inflation readings that came in higher than expected, they were broadly expected to keep the policy interest rate unchanged at 3.75%-4.00%.The Fed had raised the rate by a quarter of a percentage point in September. Most officials had indicated a need for higher interest rates, while key policymakers had also expressed willingness to wait for more data before making their next move.
Article Summary: Consumer Sentiment Index slipped to 48.0 this month from a final reading of 48.1 in September. October's reading was the second-lowest on record, following the all-time low of 44.8 recorded in May, shortly after the Iran war began. More independents and Republicans were citing high prices as a strain on their personal finances.

Article Title: Trump eases tariffs on Canadian imports weeks before US midterms, offering relief to Maine
Article Text:
The new measures will take effect on October 30.

Collins seeks relief for Maine businesses

Trade tensions strain US-Canada ties

US President Donald Trump’s administration has eased some tariffs on Canadian imports, with the move coming just two weeks before the November 3 midterm elections. The decision could benefit Republican Senator Susan Collins, who is facing a tough re-election contest in Maine, a state whose economy has been affected by the trade dispute with Canada.The White House said the changes would remove tariffs on certain products, including "plywood sheets, some paper products, certain machinery and refrigeration equipment". However, the administration will also introduce tariffs on other goods, including carpets, certain valves and waste products. The new measures will take effect on October 30.Collins said she had "secured" the exemptions for products important to Maine's agricultural sector, including blueberry, potato, apple and seaweed producers.Collins, who faces a strong challenge from a Democratic candidate, said farmers in her state depend on supplies from Canada that are difficult or expensive to source elsewhere.She said many farmers "rely on specialized equipment, packaging materials, and other products from Canada that are either unavailable from American suppliers or cannot be replaced without incurring significant expense."The senator's intervention comes as Democrats target her seat in their bid to take control of Congress from Republicans in the November 3 midterm elections.Maine shares a border with Canada, and businesses in the state have felt the effects of Trump's trade policies.The partial tariff relief could ease costs for some businesses, although the introduction of duties on other Canadian products means the changes will not benefit every sector.Also Read: After renaming Lake Ontario, Google CEO rejects US request to rename Atlantic Ocean The United States and Canada have closely connected economies, with roughly 70 per cent of Canadian exports going to the US. Trade relations have deteriorated since negotiations between the two countries broke down in August, prompting Trump to impose a fresh round of tariffs.Earlier US duties on Canadian cars, steel, aluminium and lumber have hurt businesses, contributed to job losses and weighed on economic growth. Canada entered a technical recession this year after its economy contracted for two consecutive quarters.The tariffs imposed after the collapse of trade talks affected goods worth around $20 billion, equivalent to 5.5 per cent of Canadian exports to the US. The targeted products ranged from hockey sticks to cement.Since returning to office for his second term, Trump has imposed extensive tariffs on imports from both allies and rivals, arguing that other countries have taken advantage of the United States.His administration has also linked some threatened tariffs to broader political and foreign policy goals.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump’s administration has eased some tariffs on Canadian imports. The move comes just two weeks before the November 3 midterm elections. The decision could benefit Republican Senator Susan Collins, who is facing a tough re-election contest in Maine. The new measures will take effect on October 30.

Article Title: Two critical PHP flaws trigger global alert; millions of services face cyber risk
Article Text:
Two critical PHP flaws trigger global alert.

India ranked ninth globally among services displaying PHP information.

BENGALURU: Two critical PHP vulnerabilities that could allow hackers to remotely execute code on servers without authentication have triggered a cybersecurity alert, potentially exposing millions of internet-facing services. In a separate advisory, PHP also urged users to temporarily disable a file-upload tracking feature to mitigate another remote code execution risk, adding to concerns over the widely used programming language.PHP advised users on Oct 23 to temporarily disable its session upload progress feature until the next regular bugfix release. The warning followed an earlier advisory on Oct 21 about a related vulnerability. The latest issue affects applications only when specific session settings are changed while running and the upload progress feature remains enabled. Users who have already disabled the feature do not need to take further action.The broader concerns centre on two critical vulnerabilities collectively referred to as PHP2Shell. Aamir Lakhani, global director of threat intelligence and adversarial artificial intelligence research at Fortinet, said: “Two critical PHP vulnerabilities disclosed this week pose an urgent security and business continuity risk for organizations that depend on websites, customer portals, and other web applications.PHP is a server-side programming language used by widely deployed platforms such as WordPress, Drupal, Joomla and Magento. Companies can be exposed through commercial applications, hosting providers and embedded software components even if they do not develop PHP applications themselves.The potential scale of exposure is significant. Censys identified approximately 36.7 million internet-facing services reporting potentially affected PHP versions in its Oct 22 snapshot. These are service counts, not unique servers or organisations, and may include installations already patched through vendor updates.Saeed Abbasi, head of the Threat Research Unit and director of product at Qualys, said the company found 167 million PHP package installations across 12,000 organisations, with 73% deployed on internet-facing assets, putting them within reach of remote attackers. “Applying a patch alone will not be sufficient for systems running unsupported versions, where upgrading is the only viable long-term solution. The key takeaway is that nearly all PHP installations are either vulnerable or running unsupported versions,” he said.CloudSEK said Shodan identified 2.2 million internet-facing services displaying PHP information worldwide, with India ranking ninth at 53,400 services. Of 36,700 Indian services revealing their PHP versions, about 36,100 were unpatched, including 19,500 running versions that have reached end of life, said Akash Karthi, a security researcher at CloudSEK.
Article Summary: Two critical PHP vulnerabilities that could allow hackers to remotely execute code on servers without authentication have triggered a cybersecurity alert. In a separate advisory, PHP urged users to temporarily disable a file-upload tracking feature to mitigate another remote code execution risk. The broader concerns centre on two critical vulnerabilities collectively referred to as PHP2Shell.

Article Title: Amex to cut 3,500 jobs globally despite raising 2026 profit forecast
Article Text:
American Express announced it will be laying off around 3,500 employees worldwide

American Express is cutting about 5 percent of its global workforce, affecting around 3,500 employees, as chief executive officer Steve Squeri seeks to control rising expenses and streamline operations, even as the company raises its full-year earnings forecast after reporting better-than-expected third-quarter results.According to Bloomberg, Squeri told Bloomberg TV that the company has around 78,000 employees globally. Speaking during a call with analysts on Friday, he said the job cuts were aimed at making the company more agile and efficient by reducing management layers and speeding up decision-making.The move comes amid a broader wave of workforce reductions across the financial services sector, with companies seeking to improve efficiency and, in some cases, citing the growing use of artificial intelligence.Barclays said this week it would eliminate 5,000 jobs, while HSBC is planning reductions across its UK wealth-management business. Citigroup has also been reducing its workforce.Amex announced the cuts after reporting adjusted earnings of $4.68 per share for the third quarter, beating the average analyst estimate of $4.49 in a Bloomberg survey. The company also raised its full-year 2026 earnings forecast to between $18.30 and $18.60 per share, from its earlier projection of $17.30 to $17.90.However, the company's billed business, which measures transactions on its credit cards and other products, came in at $454 billion during the quarter, below the average analyst estimate of $456.9 billion. Amex said it had exited certain small-business co-brand deals, affecting the results.Analysts at Truist Securities, including Brian Foran, described the results as mixed, noting that the earnings beat and improved guidance were positive but that slower growth in billed business was a disappointment.The company reported third-quarter expenses of $14.5 billion, an increase of about 9 percent, although the figure was below analysts' estimate of $14.8 billion. Rising costs have added to the pressure on management to improve operational efficiency while sustaining business growth.Amex's results were also affected by the sale of its equity interest in Global Business Travel Group Inc, which generated an after-tax gain of $751 million. The company used part of the proceeds to fund a $253 million after-tax restructuring charge linked to efficiency initiatives. The gain, net of the restructuring charge, was excluded from adjusted results.“Our business momentum continues, with strength in billings, new acquisitions and card member retention, and excellent credit quality,” Squeri said in a statement.The company has also been investing in its premium-card offerings. Last year, it introduced several new benefits for its Platinum card, and earlier this month announced a partnership with Airbnb that will allow certain luxury rentals booked through its travel site to qualify for cardholders' annual lodging credit.Chief financial officer Christophe Le Caillec had previously said marketing expenses were expected to rise by around 10 percent in the second half of 2026 compared with the same period last year.Separately, Amex faces a $350 million fine following enforcement actions by the US Office of the Comptroller of the Currency and the Federal Reserve over alleged deficiencies in its anti-money-laundering systems. The company said the penalty would not affect its previously issued full-year 2026 earnings guidance or its 2027 outlook. The regulatory orders also do not impose an asset cap on the company.
Article Summary: Amex announced the cuts after reporting adjusted earnings of $4.68 per share for the third quarter. Chief executive officer Steve Squeri said the job cuts were aimed at making the company more agile and efficient by reducing management layers. The move comes amid a broader wave of workforce reductions across the financial services sector.

Article Title: PHP security flaws trigger global scramble; CERT-In flags vulnerabilities
Article Text:
The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) issued a criticalseverity warning. (Reuters photo)

CERT-In Flags Vulnerabilities

BENGALURU: It has been a difficult day for cybersecurity, with critical vulnerabilities in PHP triggering an urgent global patching effort, millions of reported hacking attempts, and precautionary shutdowns of some online services. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said the scale of the incident was unusual, remarking at an event in Cologne in Germany that he had not seen anything like it “in a long, long time”.The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) issued a critical-severity warning over two vulnerabilities in PHP, a widely used open-source scripting language that powers websites and web applications. The flaws could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute malicious code remotely, disclose memory and potentially compromise affected systems.In its advisory issued on Wednesday, CERT-In said reports had confirmed large-scale exploitation in the wild and urged organisations and individuals using affected versions to apply security updates urgently.Google Cloud executives Chris Betz, chief information security officer, and Raluca Ada Popa, head of Gemini Security at Google DeepMind, said PHP and cybersecurity firm Wiz Research disclosed the two vulnerabilities after research that used multiple AI models to identify and help remediate them.Google Cloud said its own infrastructure was not vulnerable, but warned that customers running PHP applications on the platform could be exposed. It urged customers to update their applications to patched PHP versions and redeploy them. Google is also rolling out updated serverless base images for supported PHP runtimes, with automatic updates available for certain services and configurations.The scale of the response has extended beyond India. “In the 10 hours before it was publicly announced, across the network we saw thousands of attempts to exploit it,” Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince wrote in a post on X on Wednesday. Companies and govt agencies in several countries temporarily restricted access to some online services as a precaution while they worked to secure vulnerable systems.Cloudflare’s blog said it successfully deployed mitigations for all its customers after the PHP vulnerabilities were leaked before their official disclosure date. The company observed attack traffic targeting customers and tracked how attackers modified their payloads to try to bypass its security.
Article Summary: The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) issued a critical-severity warning over two vulnerabilities in PHP. The flaws could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute malicious code remotely, disclose memory and potentially compromise affected systems. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said the scale of the incident was unusual.

Article Title: Barclays to slash 5,000 jobs by 2026-end as AI takes on bigger role in bank's operations
Article Text:
Barclays to slash 5,000 jobs

Barclays plans to eliminate around 5,000 jobs, or 5% of its global workforce, by the end of this year as the British lender streamlines its operations and increases its investment in technology, including artificial intelligence (AI).The bank has already closed 1,000 positions and expects to cut another 4,000. Around 60% of the reductions are expected to affect support functions, including developers, while operational and functional roles will account for most of the job losses.The move comes as Barclays approaches the end of a three-year cost-cutting programme focused primarily on its UK retail banking business. Its investment banking division is also affected.In its third-quarter earnings presentation on Thursday, the bank said it was “structurally reducing the cost base to generate capacity for investment.” It described the expected outcome as “organisational simplification and technology change efficiency driven by AI.”Barclays said AI was the "icing on the cake" of its wider modernisation strategy. Group chief executive CS Venkatakrishnan said the job cuts reflected significant investment in technology to simplify and improve the business.Barclays reported pre-tax profit of £2.3 billion ($3.1 billion) for the three months to September, up 12% from the same period a year earlier. The figure matched forecasts compiled by LSEG, although the results were also described as slightly below forecast.Group income stood at £7.4 billion, below analysts' estimate of £7.61 billion, while net interest income was broadly unchanged at £3.91 billion.The bank's CET1 capital ratio, a measure of financial solvency, edged down to 14.2% from 14.3% at the end of the second quarter. Return on tangible equity fell to 11.7% from 16.1%.Barclays shares were almost 1% lower less than an hour into the trading session. Economists are examining company results for evidence that spending on new technology, particularly AI, is improving day-to-day operations, boosting efficiency and reducing staffing requirements.Barclays' latest workforce reduction comes amid this wider scrutiny of how companies are using AI and whether the technology is delivering operational gains.
Article Summary: Barclays plans to eliminate around 5,000 jobs, or 5% of its global workforce, by the end of this year. The bank has already closed 1,000 positions and expects to cut another 4,000. Around 60% of the reductions are expected to affect support functions.

Article Title: Meta Q3 results: Net income jumps 264% to $9.86 billion, but legal charge hits operating income
Article Text:
Meta's Q3 net income jumps 264% to $9.86 billion

Higher spending planned for AI infrastructure

Meta Platforms' net income more than tripled in the third quarter of 2026, rising 264 per cent year-on-year to $9.86 billion, as higher advertising revenue boosted its financial performance. However, a $9.89 billion legal charge pushed operating income down 37 per cent despite a 26 per cent increase in overall revenue.The company's revenue reached $64.60 billion in the quarter ended September 30, compared with $51.24 billion in the same period last year. Net income stood at $2.71 billion a year earlier, while diluted earnings per share rose to $3.83 from $1.05.Advertising remained the biggest contributor to Meta's revenue, bringing in $63.06 billion, up 26 per cent from a year ago. The number of ad impressions across its family of applications increased 10 per cent, while the average price per advertisement rose 14 per cent year-on-year.Despite the increase in revenue and net income, operating income dropped to $12.99 billion from $20.54 billion in the year-ago quarter. Total costs and expenses climbed 68 per cent to $51.61 billion, reflecting, among other expenses, a $9.89 billion charge tied to an agreement with 52 US state attorneys general to resolve litigation concerning teen mental health and social media.Meta said that excluding this charge, operating income would have been $22.88 billion. Diluted earnings per share would have reached $7.40, rather than the reported $3.83.Meta expects revenue in the fourth quarter to be between $73 billion and $76 billion. It has also revised its full-year 2026 expense outlook upwards to $175-179 billion, taking the legal charge into account.The company has increased its capital expenditure forecast for 2026 to $135-145 billion, from the previous range of $130-145 billion. The spending is part of its continued investment in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure and other business priorities.In the chief financial officer's outlook commentary, Meta said, “Our AI investments are already delivering substantial incremental advertising revenue through stronger engagement, better recommendations, and more efficient monetization.”The company said its spending on AI models and infrastructure was opening up additional revenue opportunities. However, it expects these investments to take longer to generate returns than its core business.“While these investments will take longer to generate returns than those in our core business, the breadth of monetization opportunities and internal efficiencies gives us confidence in their long-term potential,” the commentary said.Meta expects its AI investments, improvements in its models and new product launches to support strong overall revenue growth through 2027.The company is still working on its budget and capacity plans for next year as it continues to invest in AI infrastructure and pursue the revenue opportunities it expects these investments to create.
Article Summary: Meta Platforms' Q3 net income jumps 264% to $9.86 billion. Company's revenue reached $64.60 billion in the quarter ended September 30, compared with $51.24 billion in same period last year. Advertising remained the biggest contributor to Meta's revenue, bringing in $63.06 billion, up 26% from a year ago.

Article Title: 1.14 lakh startups generate more than 12 lakh jobs in India: Finance ministry
Article Text:
Finance Ministry
